thread:
anya: FYI — scheduling a targeted rolling reboot + NIC firmware reflash in us-west1 tonight 02:00-04:30 UTC. Packet-loss spikes observed after last driver bump; this should be a low-risk patch but we need coordinated drains.

devon: thanks. scope? how many racks/pools?

anya: primary impact on gradient-pool-a and burst-pool-west. ~24 GPUs total spread across 3 racks. plan is cohorted drains (rack-level), 10m drain, flash, smoke, uncordon. no full-cluster drain.

leo_oncall: I'll be on shift and will run the canaries + smoke tests. tagging @sre-bot to create incident watch.

ops-bot: Incident watch created: INC-2026-0456. Pager rotation: leo_oncall primary, devon secondary.

maria_prod: heads-up: top 2 customers have active requests in us-west1, we should pre-warn and optionally failover to eu-west if latency is sensitive.

anya: agreed — cust-success please send a short note. fallback policy: if canary fails we'll route new requests to eu-west and spin up 4 spare nodes in us-east (costy) only if needed.

cust-success: note drafted and sent to affected customers. link: https://redwood.example.com/cust-comms/INC-2026-0456

devon: quick checklist I'm proposing:
```
- 01:50 UTC: warm up cache on eu-west canary nodes (pre-seed KV cache)
- 02:00 UTC: cordon rack-3 (gradient-pool-a)
- 02:10 UTC: drain pods with eviction policy (no force unless >5m pending)
- 02:20 UTC: NIC firmware reflash script (batch of 4 devices)
- 02:28 UTC: reboot node, health-check, perf smoke (QPS + p50/p95)
- 02:35 UTC: uncordon if healthy, move to next cohort
```

devon: kubectl snippets: 
```
kubectl cordon node/<node-name>
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node-name>
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```

anya: important: do not drop active KV caches more than 2x for a tenant. we should warmup prefix cache after each cohort. I'll add a warmup job to template.

leo_oncall: can we avoid autoscaler trimming capacity during the drain? last time it started terminating spot preempts and we lost throughput.
devon: set cluster-autoscaler --balance-similar-node-groups=false for the window, and bump minReplicas for the gradient pool by +2 before starting. cost estimate ~ $120/hr for the reserved spares.

maria_prod: let's keep cost note in the thread. product OK with transient spend if we keep SLAs.

anya: canary policy: if p95 latency increases >20% or error-rate >1% for 3 consecutive checks -> abort and failover. checks run every 30s for 10 minutes after uncordon.

leo_oncall: I'll stream the smoke logs to #eng-oncall. Also will run a simple prompt workload hitting KV-heavy paths.

sre-bot: Monitor hooks added: /metrics/p95, /errors/5m, /egress/packet-loss. Alert thresholds configured.

devon: one more risk: firmware reflash sometimes leaves NIC in degraded MTU state. have a mitigation step: set MTU back to 9000 and run iperf between two nodes.

anya: note that rolling this late avoids peak for APAC; EU customers routed if we exceed thresholds. summary timeline in docs channel after this thread.

leo_oncall: starting preflight at 01:30 UTC — will ping here before cordon. if anything weird, I'll escalate to infra-oncall.

maria_prod: thanks team. I'll coordinate with legal on audit log retention for this patch (customer asked).

devon: creating patch runbook now and attaching to INC ticket.

ops-bot: Runbook attached: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/nic-reflash-2026-04

anya: final: try to keep each cohort under 25 minutes to avoid sustained tail latencies. we'll keep rolling until all 3 racks are done or we hit abort criteria. :thumbsup:

leo_oncall: acknowledged. see you at 01:30.
